answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token in a public contract before it may submit bids, with rewards and penalties settled against that deposit. The contract caps how many simultaneous bids each stake can support, so splitting funds across a swarm does not create free influence. A sybil attacker must therefore tie up real capital for the duration of a voyage and risks losing it for proven fraud; nectar and pearl can remain harmless labels, not extra identities.
